semantic_checklist.source_evidence: Inspected the attached renderings: printed p. 1 defines the constant-velocity scalar contaminant example; pp. 3–4 give (1.8), (1.10), linear flux, and the source-term conditional; pp. 4–5 distinguish classical and integral formulations.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The supplied proof-free header, readable type, explicit type, and dependency bodies describe the sourced scalar rectangle theorem.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The selected passage and inherited context are correctly located. Source and rendering hashes are supplied provenance, not independently recomputed hashes.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: Printed p. 1 uses real space and time, scalar concentration q, and constant velocity ū.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: q and production have type Real → Real → Fin 1 → Real; speed and all endpoints are real.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: A singleton-coordinate real vector faithfully represents a scalar. Speed is a single constant, not a variable coefficient. Production is an additional field supplied by the selected interpretation.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: (1.10) concerns any two spatial endpoints. The recorded convention selects rectangle balance and an almost-everywhere mass-rate identity for each fixed spatial interval.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: Rectangle identities quantify ∀ a b s t. The last conjunct is ∀ a b, ∀ᵐ t, HasDerivAt ...; the nonconservation witness is ∃ a b s t.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The temporal null set may depend on the fixed spatial interval. No common null set over all intervals is asserted, and no particular rectangle is fixed in advance.
